samples.summary: `INVALID_RESPONSE` (a 2xx that omitted the new document id) still returns exit 1, but the contract this PR implements classes a server fault as exit 2. The three import flows were converted to `exitCodeForStatus` at every HTTP-status site yet left this sibling branch — a malformed server response — as a user error, so an agent branching on `$?` sees "you typed something wrong" for a broken server. Same site in `packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:207` and `packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:250`. Either classify it as `SERVER_ERROR`/2 or record the exception in the error matrix in docs/design/cli.md §10.

Internal doc/behavior inconsistency introduced by the new error matrix: §3.4 says a failed refresh prints "Session expired. Run `wafflebase login`.", but the ~30 converted throw sites now call `httpError(res.status)` with no message, which substitutes `AUTH_FAILED_MESSAGE` ("Authentication failed. Run `wafflebase login`.") and discards the `SESSION_EXPIRED` envelope `HttpClient.sessionExpiredBody()` just built. The same 401 therefore reports `SESSION_EXPIRED` on the content/export paths (which print the body) and `AUTH_ERROR` everywhere else, and neither matches §3.4. Pick one message and make the two doc sections agree.

`PdfFontsOptions` gains a public `fetchImpl` seam in the shared `@wafflebase/docs` package, but the canonical design doc for that surface — `docs/design/docs/docs-pdf-export.md`, which explicitly documents the `PdfFontsOptions` injection seam and the `sources` override — is not updated; the new seam is described only in `docs/design/cli.md`. Per CONTRIBUTING's design-doc discipline the change to the engine package's contract belongs in the engine's own doc (nested design docs are also not link-checked by CI, so nothing else will catch the drift).

`FETCHABLE_SCHEMES` re-implements a URL scheme allowlist locally, while `packages/core/src/url/index.ts` exists precisely because per-package `isSafeUrl`/`SAFE_PROTOCOLS` copies had begun to diverge ("Hoisted here so every renderer/exporter gates hyperlinks against the same protocol allowlist"). The dereference set legitimately differs from the render set (it adds `data:`, drops `mailto:`/`tel:`), and the CLI does not currently depend on `@wafflebase/core`, so this may be acceptable — but the repo's stated pattern is that URL-safety primitives live in core, and a second hand-rolled scheme list is exactly the divergence that module was created to stop.

`GitHubAuthGuard` now throws `BadRequestException('Invalid CLI port')` for `?mode=cli` with a missing or out-of-range `port`, where previously such a request silently fell through to the ordinary web OAuth flow. rest-api.md documents the `1024–65535` range only under `/auth/github/callback`; the new hard `400` on the *authorize* endpoint (including the `mode=cli` with no `port` case, which used to be a web login) is an externally visible behavior change of a documented endpoint and is not recorded.
searchedFor: read the rest-api.md CLI auth bullets in the diff

samples.summary: Scope/approach fit: the originating task (`docs/tasks/active/20260803-cli-system-exit-code-todo.md`, issue #586) is "produce exit code 2 for system errors", with a 7-step Approach that covers only classification plumbing. This PR additionally lands two security controls (nonce-bound loopback login across backend + CLI + two design docs, and an SSRF gate with DNS pinning that adds `undici` as a new runtime dependency to a published CLI whose engine is Node ≥20) plus an unrelated API-key/`send()` refactor. The task checklist and lessons file record the decision to include them, so this is not unjustified — but it triples the review surface of a small contract fix, and the SSRF gate in particular is a self-contained control that could ship on its own.

The doc asserts "Every `fetch` in the CLI goes through `fetchOrThrow`", but `image-fetcher.ts`'s `rawRequest` issues hops through `undiciRequest` directly, wrapping failures into `SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR')` by hand. The classification outcome is the same; the absolute wording is what will be wrong the next time someone edits either side.
